extraction.name: CIFAR-10
extraction.description: A labeled subset of the tiny images dataset with 6000 examples of each of 10 classes. The paper also describes the broader tiny images dataset as 80 million downscaled 32×32 colour images collected from the web.
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The tiny images dataset was collected by colleagues at MIT and NYU over six months by searching the web for images of every non-abstract English noun in WordNet, using several search engines, keeping roughly the first 3000 results for each search term, and then removing perfect duplicates and images with excessively large white regions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Web images of non-abstract English nouns from WordNet, gathered from search engines (Google, Flickr, Altavista); the dataset contains 80 million colour images downscaled to 32 × 32 across 79,000 search terms.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: over the span of six months
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The paper says they "created two sets of reliable labels" for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, but it does not describe the actual labeling task, instructions, workforce, or QC process.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was downscaled to 32×32, perfect duplicates and images with an excessively large portion of white pixels were removed, and for some experiments the authors deleted the 1000 least-significant principal components / directions of variance.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The images were downscaled to 32×32 and whitened using a whitening matrix (ZCA whitening); for some experiments the data were further preprocessed by deleting the 1000 least-significant principal components.
